title: Environment Variables and Secrets
description: Manage database connection strings, credentials, and secrets securely across local development, preview branches, and production.

data.text: Prisma relies heavily on environment variables for sensitive settings, primarily `DATABASE_URL` and `DIRECT_URL`. Managing these correctly across environments prevents catastrophic leaks and ensures preview deployments connect to isolated databases.

data.title: File Evaluation Order
items: `.env.local`: Local developer overrides (ignored by Git, never committed).
`.env.production`: Default variables for `npm run build` and production runs.

data.title: Never Prefix Database Credentials with NEXT_PUBLIC_
data.text: In Next.js, variables prefixed with `NEXT_PUBLIC_` are inlined into the client-side JavaScript bundle and publicly visible in browser DevTools. Database connection strings must NEVER use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Never commit `.env` or `.env.local` containing passwords to Git.
Use isolated databases or branch databases (Neon / Supabase) for PR preview environments.
